finalText:
Rebase vs merge — same goal (combine branch history), different method.

**Merge**: make new commit, two parents. History stay exact as happen — both branch lines visible, plus merge commit.

**Rebase**: replay your commits one-by-one on top of target branch. New commits, new hashes. History become straight line — look like work happen sequentially, no fork ever exist.

Key differences:
- Merge: safe, non-destructive, keep true history. Rebase: rewrite history, changes commit hashes.
- Rebase on shared/pushed branch = danger. Other people history diverge, force-push needed, teammates break. Never rebase public branch.
- Merge commit clutter log with lots branch-merge noise. Rebase give clean linear log, easy `git log` read, easy bisect.

When reach for each:

- **Feature branch, local only, not pushed yet**: rebase onto main before opening PR. Clean, linear, easy review.
- **Already pushed, others pulled it**: merge. Don't rewrite shared history.
- **Want preserve exact record of when branches diverge/joined** (audit trail matter): merge.
- **Want clean bisectable history, small team, force-push private branch OK**: rebase workflow (rebase then fast-forward merge).
- **Conflict resolution**: rebase = resolve conflict per-commit, can get repetitive on long branch. Merge = resolve once, in single merge commit.

Rule of thumb: rebase *before* share (clean local work), merge *when* integrate shared/public work.
